tasks.short: Write activity budgets from last period costs and this period's allowed spend.

steps.what: Read last period costs for the recreational activities
Add those activity costs into the budgets workbook
Write the budgets for the programs she will run
Agree those budgets with her manager before the season

tasks.design: A configured report on the {ERP} groups recorded cost lines by the activity code she named and adds the amounts into the budget workbook. She still writes this period's allowed spend for each program and agrees those budgets with her manager. A model does not write the amounts or any commentary.
tasks.previous_blocker: The cost totals already sat in the ledger, but she retyped each one into the budget workbook by hand before she could set the allowed spend.
tasks.enabler_now: The ledger already stores activity code, cost centre and amount, so a configured grouping can add the amounts without a separate list of codes.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing this period's allowed spend, and agreeing it with her manager, stays her judgement.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which program should receive more money this season and which cost should not be repeated.

ambition.what: She sets the allowed spend for each activity in the same sitting as the grouped costs, on every program she writes that month, before the meeting.

tasks.altitude: She still sets the allowed spend and still agrees it with her manager. The retyping of cost totals into the workbook is the part that goes.

reach.task: Write a treatment-room budget from last period's costs.
reach.learn: A grouped cost total is not the allowed spend.

evidence.claim: Grouping recorded cost lines that already carry an activity code, then adding the amounts, is arithmetic. Setting this period's allowed spend is not.

A review of an Australian welfare compliance system, priced A$439,000 and partly drafted with a model, cited non-existent sources and a fabricated court case. The firm agreed to repay the final instalment.

assumptions: The {ERP} already stores cost centre, activity code and amount on each recorded cost line. Finance posting produced those lines. This task does not create them.
When a line has no activity code, she types the code while she reads the lines in s1, and that time stays in s1.
No separate code list is maintained, so incremental hours are zero.
The budget is not sent outside the organisation. The meeting with her manager is not a versioned send, and nothing is filed as a further step.
Stop the grouping if a total is a named person's wage.
unknowns: How often a recorded cost line has no activity code.
Whether any grouped total is a named person's wage.
research_questions: Which cost-centre totals in this venue are wages of a named person, and must stay out of the grouping?

already_counted.description: Writing the allowed spend for each program is the judgement inside s3 and is already in that step's remaining time.

incremental.description: No code list or commentary text is kept up. Missing activity codes are typed inside s1, so extra hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A short season with few activity codes is about 4 percent. A summer program with many recorded cost lines is about 9 percent. She still writes every allowed amount.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with coworkers on radios and computers during the day.

steps.what: Hear coworkers on the radios during the day
Answer those coworkers on the radios

tasks.design: Nothing is drafted or sent. She hears coworkers on the radio and answers on the radio or on the computer. The talk stays hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: The reply depends on what she hears in the moment, and a stored message is not a substitute for answering.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new makes the talk shorter. The radio and the computer stay the means she uses herself.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the floor and answering in her own words stays the whole task.
tasks.human_edge: She hears tone and urgency on the radio and decides the reply while the coworker is waiting.
tasks.altitude: Her week of radio and computer replies is unchanged. She still answers both herself.

reach.task: Tell floor staff a changed class time.
reach.learn: The radio reply stays with the person who hears the call.

evidence.claim: The task is the radio exchange and the computer reply. This design does not shorten either one.

assumptions: Coworker replies stay inside the organisation, so they are internal writes, not external sends.
No list, stock text, or tool is maintained for the replies, so incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether any computer reply goes to a person outside the organisation.
research_questions: Which computer messages, if any, leave the organisation and would need their own send step?

incremental.description: No list or stock text is kept for radio or computer replies, so extra hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The talk is the task, so the saving is zero in a quiet week and in a busy week.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tell customers about events and activities at the facility.

steps.what: Hear which events the customers ask about
Tell those customers the events and the activities

tasks.design: Nothing is drafted or sent. She hears which events a visitor asks about and tells them the events and the activities in person. The words stay hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visitors ask in person, and the useful answer is the one she speaks then.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new makes the spoken answer shorter. She already holds the event facts from planning.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the question and telling the visitor stays the whole task.
tasks.human_edge: She hears what the visitor actually needs and says the part of the event that answers it.
tasks.altitude: The desk conversation is unchanged. She still tells visitors herself.

reach.task: Tell a visitor what an event includes.
reach.learn: The spoken facts stay with the person at the desk.

evidence.claim: The task is the spoken telling of events and activities. This design does not shorten it.

assumptions: Event facts she tells are ones she already holds from planning. This task does not create them.
The answer is spoken, not a later message, so there is no versioned send to gate.
No list or tool is maintained for the talk, so incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether she also sends a written follow-up after the spoken answer.
research_questions: Does any visitor question get a written reply later, and would that reply need its own send step?

incremental.description: No list or stock wording is kept for visitor answers, so extra hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The spoken answer is the task, so the saving is zero on a quiet day and on a busy day.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan which events and activities run, and when each room is free.

steps.what: Agree which events belong in the programs
Write each activity, room and date for those programs
Place those activities on the schedules without a room clash
Keep or change a program after reading the placed schedules

tasks.design: She names each activity, room and date. A configured rule on the {CALENDAR} refuses a second booking of the same room at the same time, using bookings already on the calendar. She still chooses the events and still keeps or changes the program. Named staff are not assigned here.
tasks.previous_blocker: She tried room times by hand against bookings she already had, and a clash showed up only after she had written the line.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking rows already store activity, room, start and end, so a configured rule can refuse a second booking of the same room at the same time.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which events belong, and keeping or dropping one after she sees the times, stays her judgement.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which event should run even when the room is free, and which one should not.

ambition.what: In the planning meeting she sees which activities share a room and a time, and she keeps or moves them before the meeting ends.

tasks.altitude: She still chooses the events and still keeps or changes the program. Trying room times that already clash is the part that goes.

reach.learn: A refused double booking is not a decision about which class should run.

evidence.claim: A booking can be refused when another activity already holds the same room at the same time. Choosing which events belong in the program cannot be done by that rule.
Works-council consent is required for rosters and for staff-data and loss-prevention monitoring of staff.

assumptions: A booking row already has activity, room, start and end. She writes those on the activity lines in s2. Existing bookings are prior rows, not created in s3.
No room-to-activity list is maintained apart from the lines she writes, so incremental hours are zero.
The rule does not write staff names, so this is not a roster and not a staff decision.
The program is not published from this task, so there is no external send to gate.
unknowns: Whether every booking row already has a room, a start and an end.
Whether anyone expects staff names on the program.
research_questions: If staff names were added to the room rule later, would the works council treat that rule as a roster?

already_counted.description: Reading the placed times and keeping or changing the program is the judgement inside s4 and is already in that step's remaining time.

incremental.description: No room list is kept apart from the activity lines she writes in s2, so extra hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Two rooms and a few activities are about 4 percent. A holiday program with many rooms is about 9 percent. She still chooses the events and still reads the result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still sets what the facility will spend, still answers the radio and the visitors, and still chooses which events run. Less time goes to retyping cost totals into a budget workbook and to trying room times that already clash.
reach: Spa Managers writing a treatment-room budget from last period's costs should learn that a grouped cost total is not the allowed spend.

Fitness and Wellness Coordinators telling floor staff a changed class time should learn the radio reply stays with the person who hears the call, and that a refused double booking is not a decision about which class should run.
Fundraising Managers telling a visitor what an event includes should learn the spoken facts stay with the person at the desk.
skills_to_grow: Name the activity code before a cost total is grouped, and still write the allowed spend herself.
Leave the radio reply and the visitor answer as her own words.
Write the room and the time on each activity line, and still drop an event that should not run.
role.ambitious_version: On the morning she writes a program she sees which activities share a room, and she sees last period's cost beside the spend she will allow, before the meeting. She still chooses the events, still sets the spend, and still tells visitors herself. She does not let a cost total stand as the budget, and she does not assign named staff when the room times are placed.

job.title: Entertainment and Recreation Managers, Except Gambling
